newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares inch up on cements and bank trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares inch up on cements and bank trade.

text.p: Selective trade in blue-chip cement and bank stocks failed to strengthen Egyptian share prices significantly on Thursday.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index rose 0.13 points to close at 333.64 in average volume of 42.5 million pounds ($12.5 million).
"The market today was very selectively traded and there was concentrated volume in a few select stocks," said broker Tareq Lotfy of Intercapital Brokerage.

Lotfy said the activity could be attributed to investors buying the cheaper local shares in Suez Cement and Commercial International Bank (CIB) to convert into global depository receipts which are listed in London.

CIB closed 0.3 pounds higher at 71.3 after shares worth 3.2 million pounds changed hands and Suez Cement, which maintained healthy trade this week, slipped 0.2 to 63.8 pounds in 2.8 million pounds worth of trade.
Trade in Amriyah Cement, the day's most active stock, was worth 4.2 million pounds. It fell 0.4 to 80.5 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 444.12 points from 444.96 points on Wednesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 250.21 from 249.84 points.
Of the 91 shares traded, 36 rose, 38 ended lower and 17 remained unchanged.
